items.title: US ambassador says Israel not planning forced displacement from Gaza
items.description: The US ambassador to Israel said on Saturday there was no plan underway to force Palestinians out of Gaza, after Israeli ministers laid out ideas on how to expel the war-battered territory’s two million people. “I can tell you categorically there is no plan of the Israelis to displace people out of Gaza against their will,” Ambassador Mike Huckabee told reporters as he visited Palestinian-Americans in the Israeli-occupied West Bank. Israeli far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir laid out a plan on Thursday that aims to see the departure of 250,000 Palestinians from Gaza in the first year, followed by the rest of the roughly two million residents over the following six years. His remarks came a day after Defence Minister Israel Katz said Israel was ready to remove Palestinians from Gaza by sea and land but was waiting for the United States, which he said was discussing where the population would go. Katz, without citing his source, claimed 80 per cent of people in Gaza wanted to leave but that Hamas was preventing them. Huckabee said that President Donald Trump’s administration — which has made hostility to international migration a central priority — wanted to give Palestinians the option to leave by choice. “There is an open-mindedness if people wish to leave, that they should have the right to leave,” Huckabee said, calling it a “disgrace” to “incarcerate” Palestinians inside Gaza. “Nobody is suggesting there would be forced displacement — the Israelis are not, the Americans are not. I know of no one who supports that,” he said. Forced displacement of a civilian population from occupied territory is considered a war crime under the Geneva Conventions. Virtually the entire population of Gaza has already been displaced internally by Israel’s military offensive following the Hamas-led Oct 7, 2023 attack on Israel. Since the war, some far-right Israeli politicians have spoken of bringing settlers back to the Gaza Strip, where Israel dismantled settlements in 2005 as part of a unilateral plan to disengage from the densely populated region. The remarks on displacement come in the run-up to the October 27 elections, in which polls show a tight race for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who has brought once-shunned far-right figures into his cabinet. US President Donald Trump stunned the world early in his second term by proposing to displace all Palestinians at least temporarily from Gaza and turn the rubble-strewn Mediterranean territory into a luxury resort . He backtracked after pushback from countries including Egypt, the only country other than Israel to border Gaza. Israel has ‘responsibility’ to ensure safety of West Bank Palestinians The US ambassador to Israel also said that the Israeli government bore responsibility for West Bank Palestinians’ safety and should impose “severe consequences” over violence, as he visited families after a surge in settler attacks. Mike Huckabee, long known as a staunch supporter of Israel and settlers, visited a Palestinian-American’s home in the West Bank that has been repeatedly targeted by settlers and said he wanted to hear the community’s “legitimate grievances”. As the ambassador met families inside a finely manicured old house in the town of Turmus Ayya , where around 80pc of the 4,000 residents hold US citizenship, a settler from a nearby illegal outpost approached in a quad bike. “One of the messages that we have been sending and we will continue to send is that people in these communities have a right to live with a level of security and safety, and that the government has a responsibility to make sure that that happens,” Huckabee said. Israel has occupied the West Bank since 1967 and violence by Israeli settlers towards Palestinian residents has persisted for years, often with little or no legal consequence, but recent months have seen a surge in attacks ahead of October 27 elections. Huckabee stopped short of criticising Israel by name but said: “Our clear message is that crime is crime, terror is terror. “When people do it they should have an expectation that they will have severe consequences,” Huckabee said. He said that taking action was in the “best interest” of Israel, which already faces growing criticism around the world, including in key ally the United States, over the devastating offensive in Gaza in response to the Oct 7, 2023 Hamas attack. “Their reputation does not do well when it appears that this tiny little group of marauders are somehow representative of the larger population. I don’t believe that it is,” Huckabee said. “There may be a few hundred who are responsible, but that’s a few hundred too many,” Huckabee said. ‘US has the ability’ “We have many issues that we will address,” Nawwaf Zaghoul, the town’s mayor, told reporters ahead of the meeting, describing what he said were constant attacks by settlers. He said that the town’s residents would be asking the ambassador to help secure their safety and security. About 80 per cent of the town’s roughly 3,000 residents were Palestinian Americans, he said. US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee is greeted by members of the local municipality as he arrives to visit the home of an American-Palestinian resident who has previously been twice attacked and faces ongoing harassment from Israeli settlers, in the Israeli-occupied West Bank town of Turmus Ayya, about 23 kilometers northeast of Ramallah, where a large proportion of the town’s residents hold dual nationality on Sept 5, 2026. — AFP Huckabee spent about two hours meeting Palestinian-Americans inside the home of Samir Hazmeh before joining the community in a lunch of maqluba , a dish of rice and meat served after flipping the pot upside down. Hazmeh said the house in which he welcomed Huckabee had its windows smashed twice by settlers, who have also tried to open the gates and burn it down. He has put up both barbed wire and an American flag in hopes of protection. Yasser Alqam, who met the ambassador, owns land just 100 metres away but said he cannot return after several attacks by settlers. “The United States already has the ability to put pressure on Israel to at least arrest those settlers who are known to the authorities,” he said, voicing shock that US President Donald Trump lifted sanctions on settler extremists imposed by predecessor Joe Biden. Alqam’s wife Jinan, wearing a traditional Palestinian dress, said she voiced hope to Huckabee that he “can do something for us and provide us with protection from the settlers so that we can reach our land and pick the olives” in the coming season. Huckabee also visited Taybeh, one of the only Christian villages remaining in the West Bank, in June 2025 after a church there was vandalised . Huckabee said at the time that the desecration of a place of worship was an act of terror and a crime. ‘Thou shalt not steal’ Ahead of elections, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s government has been ramping up approval of new settlements, which are illegal under international law. More than 500,000 Israelis live in the West Bank amid three million Palestinians. Despite Huckabee’s dismissal of violent settlers as a small minority, Netanyahu has brought into his government far-right ministers who have openly mused about expelling the Palestinian population. Huckabee, an evangelical Christian pastor and former governor of Arkansas, has long cited his faith to back Israel and earlier would not even use the term Palestinian. Speaking of violence by settlers, Huckabee said, “I think the Scripture is pretty clear — Thou shalt not steal, thou shalt not kill, and thou shalt not even covet.” Huckabee earlier intervened when settler extremists camped out and blocked basic supplies from reaching another Palestinian-American in the town of Qusra last month, leading to rare condemnation by Netanyahu of settlers. Huckabee refers to the West Bank by its biblical name, Judea and Samaria, a term used by the Israeli government but not adopted by the US government. He has visited Shiloh, a settlement near Turmus Ayya, at least twice since 2025. In February, Huckabee drew widespread condemnation from at least 14 countries , including Pakistan, after he suggested that he would not be opposed to Tel Aviv taking over large swathes of the Middle East.

items.title: UEFA-FIFA : le Maroc au cœur des soupçons de malversations visant Infantino
items.description: Le Maroc est décidément un pays qui tente de s’acheter en tout, y compris en football. Le royaume est cité dans le conflit opposant le président de la FIFA et la confédération européenne UEFA. Selon la presse marocaine, Gianni Infantino a tenté de monnayer des soutiens pour sa réélection, dont celui du Maroc. La finale de la Coupe du Monde 2030 au Maroc contre un soutien à la réélection d’Infantino Dans son mémoire adressé fin août dernier à la justice américaine pour réunir des preuves contre Infantino, l’UEFA a accusé ce dernier d’avoir cherché à soudoyer la fédération marocaine, rapporte le site Le Desk. Selon le document, le président de la FIFA , pour assurer sa réélection à la tête de l’instance footballistique mondiale, a promis à la fédération marocaine d'organiser au Maroc la finale de la Coupe du monde 2030, qui sera co-organisée par le royaume avec l’Espagne et le Portugal. Pour cela, il a exigé la publication d’une déclaration de soutien à sa candidature. Le Maroc, illustration de la méthode du président de la FIFA Le Maroc est cité comme l’ “illustration d'une méthode que l'UEFA impute au président de la FIFA, celle de mobiliser des attributions de compétitions comme instrument de politique interne”, écrit Le Desk. Une méthode qui ne date pas d’aujourd'hui. En 2018 déjà, lors de l’attribution de l’organisation du Mondial 2026, Infantino aurait, “tout en affichant une posture de neutralité”, favorisé en réalité le dossier nord-américain et démarché des chefs d'État étrangers “pour lui trouver des voix”, accuse l’UEFA. La candidature des États-Unis, du Canada et du Mexique l'avait emporté par 134 voix contre 34 pour la candidature marocaine. Cette fois, c’est le Maroc que le patron controversé de la FIFA aurait cherché à soudoyer au détriment de l’Espagne qui revendique le droit d’abriter la finale du prochain mondial. Le Maroc est clairement désigné dans le document comme un “soutien monnayé” de Gianni Infantino. La requête de l’UEFA auprès de la justice américaine vise à réunir des preuves en vue d’une plainte au pénal devant la justice suisse contre le président de la FIFA. L’article UEFA-FIFA : le Maroc au cœur des soupçons de malversations visant Infantino est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.description: The Joy FM Back-to-School Discount Fair has entered its final day at the Joy FM Car Park in Kokomlemle, Accra, with shoppers continuing to take advantage of discounted prices on a wide range of school essentials. Parents, guardians and students have been visiting the fairgrounds to purchase items ahead of the reopening of schools. From books and stationery to school bags, shoes, clothing, electronics, sanitary products and other household essentials, the fair has provided shoppers with the opportunity to find several items in one convenient location. items.title: GB CM constitutes committee to review trekking rules after deadly Broad Peak avalanche
items.description: GILGIT: Gilgit-Baltistan Chief Minister Amjad Hussain has constituted a three-member committee to review the 1999 Trekking Rules and Regulations, according to a statement issued by the CM House on Saturday, a few weeks after 10 mountaineers lost their lives when an avalanche struck on Broad Peak . The 10 members were part of an expedition led by world-renowned British-Nepali mountaineer Nirmal Purja . They were struck by the avalanche on July 30. Purja’s company later announced that there were no survivors. CM Hussain expressed deep concern over multiple accidents during mountaineering activities this year, which claimed the lives of 13 foreign and two Pakistani climbers. In another recent accident, Pakistani clim­ber Asma Mushtaq , 34, died on GB’s Spantik Peak on Aug 20 while desc­ending from the mountain after suffering from high-altitude sickness. A ground team recovered her body on Monday, almost 10 days after her death on the 7,027-metre-tall mountain. The GB chief minister has directed the committee to review the relevant procedures, terms and conditions, and standard operating procedures (SOPs) for dealing with mountaineering incidents. It has also been tasked with determining responsibility for any negligence or administrative lapses in the delayed rescue operations following recent accidents. The committee will be headed by Forest, Wildlife and Parks Secretary Subtain Ahmed, with Information Technology Secretary Zameer Abbas and Baltistan Division Commissioner Kamal Khan serving as members. The CM has further directed the committee to determine responsibility for any shortcomings in the Broad Peak incident, conduct a clause-by-clause review of the existing trekking regulations, and identify outdated, ineffective or incomplete provisions. He also directed the relevant institutions to ensure the safety and security of mountaineers, trekking groups, guides and porters. A source told Dawn that complaints had been submitted to CM Hussain regarding negligence and delay in rescue operations. CM Hussain said it was essential to update regulations concerning permits and registration, briefing and debriefing, the responsibilities of liaison officers and mountain guides, safety equipment, porters’ wages and welfare, insurance, medical facilities and evacuation, communication systems, and emergency response procedures. He specifically directed a review of the existing insurance coverage for liaison officers, mountain guides and porters, adding that realistic and effective insurance coverage should be proposed in view of current risks and costs. He further directed the committee to review arrangements for search and rescue, helicopter evacuation, weather forecasting and early warning systems, communications, and emergency assistance in remote and restricted areas. CM Hussain tasked the committee with developing mandatory safety protocols to minimise the risk of loss of life in the future. The chief minister said that, given the growing popularity of trekking and mountaineering in Gilgit-Baltistan, the existing classification of open and restricted zones, as well as various trekking routes and mountain passes, should also be updated in accordance with ground realities. He said a digital permit and registration system, effective coordination among relevant institutions, and periodic reviews of laws governing the trekking and mountaineering sector were now essential. CM Hussain also reiterated that the GB government would promote mountaineering and tourism in the region without compromising the safety and security of tourists, mountaineers, guides and porters. The committee has been directed to submit a comprehensive report, recommendations and a draft of the proposed amendments to the laws and SOPs to the relevant authority within 15 days. The committee has not yet submitted its report. A government official familiar with the region’s tourism industry told Dawn that the committee had found some tour operators responsible for violating mountaineering rules during the expedition. According to the official, some tour operators had failed to arrange insurance for climbers or helicopters in case of a rescue operation. “Under the rules, if a ground rescue team or helicopter is needed, the tour operator is responsible for arranging a rescue team and paying for helicopter insurance,” the source said. Some operators had also failed to conduct the briefing and debriefing sessions required under the 1999 Trekking Rules, according to the official. In a recent statement, the Alpine Club of Pakistan (ACP) said that search-and-rescue operations relied on government resources, adding that Pakistan lacks a dedicated and properly established high-altitude rescue system. The ACP said that it was working with relevant authorities to develop an effective rescue framework and support improvements to the country’s mountaineering infrastructure. More than 2,200 foreign climbers and trekkers visited GB during the summer season from April to August this year, a senior official of the GB Tourism Department said. Sajid Hussain, deputy director of the GB Tourism Department, told Dawn that foreign adventurers visited the region to scale some of the world’s highest peaks and trek in restricted areas, including K2 (8,611 metres), Nanga Parbat (8,126m), Broad Peak (8,047m), Gasherbrum-I (8,080m) and Gasherbrum-II (8,035m). The official added that a large number of foreign and domestic tourists were currently visiting popular destinations across GB. Foreign tourists visiting open-zone areas do not require permits. Officials further said foreign tourists visiting GB’s tourist destinations and open-zone areas from multiple countries during the spring, summer and autumn seasons were expected to surpass 10,000 this year. GB Tourism Department’s Hussain said the number of foreign adventurers visiting GB this summer was higher than last year . As of June 30, the GB government had earned Rs350 million from expedition and trekking pe­­rmits for this summer.

items.title: INEC offers biometric support to JAMB
items.description: By Olayinka Ajayi The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, has expressed its readiness to support the Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board, JAMB, with biometric verification technology as part of efforts to deepen collaboration between the two federal agencies. Speaking during a courtesy visit to the INEC headquarters in Abuja at the weekend, JAMB Registrar, Prof. Segun Aina, led members of the board’s management team and said JAMB approached INEC as a sister agency with considerable experience in the deployment of biometric technology for the identification and verification of large numbers of Nigerians. He said the Board was seeking to further strengthen the integrity of its examination processes and had learned that INEC had biometric verification equipment that might no longer be in active use. Aina therefore appealed to the Commission to consider making some of the equipment available to JAMB to support its efforts to enhance biometric verification. Responding, INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, SAN, welcomed the delegation and commended JAMB for its statutory responsibilities, describing the Board as a critical institution in Nigeria’s education system and the development of the country’s youth. The Chairman received the delegation alongside the National Commissioner in charge of Outreach and Partnerships, Prof. Abdullahi Abdu-Zuru; the Directors of Information and Communications Technology (ICT), Dr. Lawrence Bayode; Human Resources Management, Umar M. Bashar; and Voter Education and Publicity (VEP), Mrs Victoria Eta-Messi; as well as the Chief Press Secretary to the Chairman, Adedayo Oketola. Amupitan said INEC’s recent electoral engagements, including the Anambra and Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Area Council elections, the Ekiti and Osun governorship elections, as well as bye-elections conducted across the country, had further demonstrated the Commission’s growing technological capacity. According to him, the deployment of technology in recent elections had attracted commendations from stakeholders, including the Office of the National Security Adviser and the United Kingdom High Commission, particularly for the credibility and peaceful conduct of the exercises. The INEC Chairman directed the Director of ICT to review JAMB’s request and undertake a proof-of-concept assessment to determine the availability, technical condition and suitability of any biometric verification equipment that could potentially be deployed by the Board. He described the visit as a reflection of the growing importance of inter-agency collaboration and the need for government institutions to leverage their respective expertise and resources in advancing national development. Amupitan assured the JAMB delegation that INEC remained willing to explore further areas of cooperation that could strengthen the capacity of both institutions to deliver on their respective mandates. In his response, Aina expressed appreciation to the INEC Chairman and management for the warm reception accorded him and his team, reaffirming JAMB’s interest in strengthening institutional collaboration with the Commission. items.title: When war takes more than territory: The human cost of conflict
items.description: The return of children, detained civilians and prisoners of war remains a critical test for international diplomacy. Battles, territory and military operations often define wars. But their greatest impact is felt by people whose lives are disrupted by displacement, separation and detention. In Ukraine, Russia’s war has created a serious humanitarian challenge. Children have been separated from their families, civilians detained, and prisoners of war held away from their homes. At the centre of international efforts is a simple question: Who gets to go home? Children are among the most vulnerable victims of war. Separation from parents and communities can affect their education, identity and wellbeing. Their safe return requires cooperation among governments, international organisations and humanitarian groups. For families of detained civilians, uncertainty can be equally devastating. Information about missing relatives can offer hope, while diplomatic engagement can help create opportunities for their release. Prisoners of war are protected by international humanitarian law. Respecting these protections remains essential, regardless of the wider political context of a conflict. Diplomacy can help address these humanitarian concerns even when broader political negotiations are difficult. Identifying missing people, exchanging information and facilitating safe returns can be important steps towards rebuilding trust. The international community must ensure that humanitarian concerns remain central to discussions on Ukraine. Peace should mean more than an end to fighting. It should also mean families reuniting, children protected, civilians released, and prisoners of war safely returned home. The success of diplomacy should therefore be measured not only by agreements between governments but also by the lives those efforts help to restore. Because peace is ultimately about giving people the chance to return home and to rebuild their lives.

The intervention followed the August 22 fire outbreak at the shopping mall, which affected several businesses and destroyed properties worth billions of naira, leaving business owners with substantial losses. Receiving the First Lady, Governor Bassey Otu expressed appreciation to President Tinubu and Senator Tinubu for the intervention, describing it as a timely gesture that would bring succour to victims of the fire disaster. items.title: Review SHS placement policy to give more BECE candidates access – Kwesi Kwarteng
items.description: Former Ministry of Education Public Relations Officer, Kwesi Kwarteng, has urged the government to review the current Senior High School (SHS) placement criteria to create opportunities for more BECE candidates to continue their education. He is particularly advocating a gradual reversal of the requirement that candidates must pass both English Language and Mathematics to qualify for placement in Senior High Schools (SHSs) and Senior High Technical Schools (SHTSs). His call follows the exclusion of nearly 55,000 candidates who sat for the 2026 Basic Education Certificate Examination (BECE) from the SHS/SHTS placement process. According to the Coordinator of the Computerised School Selection and Placement System (CSSPS) Secretariat, Sherif Sulemana, approximately 565,000 out of the nearly 620,000 candidates who took the examination met the requirements for placement. But speaking on Channel One TV’s The Big Issue, Mr Kwarteng argued that the number of candidates left out should not automatically be interpreted as evidence that they failed the BECE. He attributed much of the exclusion to the placement criteria currently being applied by the government. “My point is that if you look at the 54,000 [about 55,000] students that have been denied access to the senior high schools, it has nothing to do with students failing necessarily, but has more to do with the placement policy that this government is using. “Instead of creating barriers that limit students and prevent access for those students, I think we should be very progressive and reverse back to the earlier placement policies that we have,” he said. Calls for return to previous criteria Mr Kwarteng explained that under the previous NPP administration, students who failed one of the two subjects but passed the other could still secure placement and receive the opportunity to improve their performance at the secondary level. “When we were in government, the placement policy that we were using was that if a student fails English and passes Mathematics, that student is given an opportunity to proceed to the senior high to justify himself,” he said. “If a student fails Mathematics but passes English, the student is given an opportunity to justify himself,” he added. He said the current requirement has effectively introduced a stricter condition that prevents candidates from progressing if they fail either of the two subjects. “But the current situation is that if you fail either English or Mathematics, you are not given an opportunity. In our case, what was happening is that if you pass any one of them, you go. But this time, they are saying that you have to pass the two,” Mr Kwarteng said. According to him, the policy risks shutting out students who may have the capacity to perform well at the SHS level if given the chance. “I am not a fan of systems and policies that intentionally set barriers for ordinary Ghanaian students,” he said. Pass in one core subject should be enough Mr Kwarteng proposed that candidates who demonstrate competence in at least one of the two subjects should be allowed to proceed to secondary school. “So that if you pass either English or Mathematics, you are given the opportunity. And this time around, this whole policy about you having to pass the two of them is just a policy that the government has introduced,” he said. He further suggested that the current criteria could be functioning as an indirect cut-off mechanism, potentially aimed at controlling the number of students entering SHS amid concerns over the cost of providing secondary education. Mr Kwarteng argued that the debate should therefore go beyond students’ examination results and examine the policy decisions determining access to secondary education. “It is not the student performing; it is a government discriminatory policy that has caused a barrier,” he said. Education policy should create opportunities The former Education Ministry PRO also drew comparisons with tertiary education, arguing that students who fall short of certain academic requirements in Ghana can sometimes perform successfully when given opportunities to study elsewhere. He cited instances where students with D7 grades who are unable to gain admission to universities in Ghana have secured places at institutions outside the country and subsequently returned to Ghana to practise professionally. For him, such examples demonstrate the importance of creating pathways that allow students to develop their abilities instead of permanently shutting them out based on a single academic requirement. Mr Kwarteng also questioned whether financial considerations were influencing the government’s approach to SHS placement. He expressed doubts about whether the government could completely eliminate the double-track system while simultaneously expanding access to secondary education. He argued that if the government is using placement restrictions to manage expenditure, it should be open about the reasons behind the policy. “The entire aim is that if we cannot get so much money to take care of students at the senior high school level, we made so much noise about double track,” he said. Mr Kwarteng therefore reiterated his call for a review of the placement requirements, insisting that students who pass at least one of the two core subjects should be given an opportunity to continue their education at the SHS level.

items.title: Tano South Municipal Assembly moves to curb road carnage with speed ramps
items.description: The Tano South Municipality in the Ahafo Region is taking decisive action to address a growing public safety crisis on its major highways. For months, excessive speeding due to a lack of speed-calming measures has turned transit corridors in the area into hazard zones, causing severe crashes, loss of life, destroyed property, and immense strain on local healthcare facilities, particularly the Bechem Government Hospital. Delivering his sessional address at the second ordinary meeting of the third session of the ninth assembly on Thursday, September 3, 2026, in Bechem, the Municipal Chief Executive (MCE), Emmanuel Kwame Frimpong, noted that to address the persistent road safety threats, the assembly has approved the construction of speed ramps along high-speed corridors passing through major townships, specifically Bechem, Techimantia, and Dwomoh. In addition to physical traffic interventions, the assembly is taking aim at local revenue leaks. The MCE indicated that there will be a strict crackdown on unauthorized revenue checkpoints across the municipality, with a strong enforcement focus on Techimantia to ensure municipal tax collection is secure, legitimate, and properly accounted for. According to global data from the World Health Organization, road traffic accidents cause approximately 1.19 million deaths each year, with excessive or inappropriate speeding identified as a direct factor in nearly one-third of all global road fatalities. Africa faces the highest road traffic fatality rate of any continent, suffering approximately 26.6 deaths per 100,000 people despite holding only 3 per cent of the world’s registered motor vehicles, with unmonitored vehicle speeds serving as a main driver of fatal crashes. In Ghana, the National Road Safety Authority (NRSA) records show that excessive speeding accounts for over 50 per cent to 60 per cent of all national road traffic collisions. Uncontrolled speeds on highways passing through rural towns and market centers account for thousands of severe injuries and fatalities annually across the country. The consequences of unmonitored highway speeds spill over into every aspect of community well-being, healthcare, and economic security. The loss of life and severe injuries frequently target breadwinners and youth, devastating household incomes and leaving families without primary caregivers. From an economic perspective, traffic crashes siphon away between 3 per cent and 5 per cent of developing nations’ annual GDP in medical bills, property destruction, and lost workplace productivity. At the local level, severe highway collisions overstretch emergency resources at healthcare facilities like the Bechem Government Hospital, depleting blood banks, overwhelming trauma units, and straining daily medical operations. Property damage is equally severe, as high-speed crashes routinely ruin vehicles, smash public roadside utility poles, and destroy private shops and structures along transit corridors. Traffic safety studies across developing road networks confirm that physical speed humps and ramps are among the most immediate, cost-effective infrastructure upgrades for town-transit highways. In Ghana, field research indicates that implementing properly engineered speed humps in township zones can reduce fatal and serious casualty crashes by 70 per cent to 77 per cent. By forcing long-distance transit traffic to slow down from highway speeds of 80 to 100 km/h to safe settlement limits of 30 to 50 km/h, speed ramps give pedestrians, particularly schoolchildren, traders, and elderly residents a drastically higher survival rate when crossing main roads. Complementing the assembly’s traffic and revenue initiatives, the Member of Parliament for Tano South, Charles Asiedu, highlighted major infrastructure progress for rural communities. He emphasized that a total of 18 communities across the constituency, including Mansopa, Asikasu, Mawoaninso, Asuboe, Nyamebeye, Wuraponho, Bredi, Ninkyininkyi, Nsuta, Kyebi, Nyamebekyere, Asukoko, among others, are scheduled for connection to the national electricity grid. Mr Asiedu stated that the electrification push is set to drive local commercial activity, provide power for students studying at night, and improve nighttime visibility to deter criminal activity across the municipality.

items.title: Écoles pionnières : le ministère tranche la question des heures supplémentaires
items.description: Le ministère de l'Éducation nationale, de l'Enseignement primaire et du Sport vient de mettre fin aux incertitudes entourant la gestion du soutien scolaire prolongé au sein des « Écoles pionnières » pour l'année scolaire 2026/27. Dans une note officielle adressée ce vendredi 4 septembre aux directeurs des Académies régionales de l'éducation et de la formation (AREF), la tutelle a confirmé le maintien des heures supplémentaires rémunérées pour les enseignants volontaires, tout en s'engageant à débloquer les budgets nécessaires au paiement de leurs indemnités. Afin d'encadrer la généralisation de ce dispositif, le ministère a fixé des directives claires. L'extension du soutien pédagogique ne devra en aucun cas conduire au regroupement de classes ni engendrer de surcapacité dans les salles de cours. La note insiste sur une rationalisation des ressources humaines et une optimisation des emplois du temps afin de garantir le déroulement normal des enseignements tout en assurant une couverture efficace des besoins des élèves. Sur le plan financier et logistique, la mesure rassure le corps enseignant. La possibilité d'effectuer des heures supplémentaires reste ouverte à l'ensemble des professeurs, qu'ils soient chargés des matières fondamentales ou dédiés au soutien prolongé, sur la base du volontariat et selon les barèmes d'indemnisation en vigueur. Le ministère précise d'ailleurs que les crédits budgétaires requis pour le règlement de ces prestations seront inscrits à la programmation financière de l'exercice 2027, dans la continuité des exercices précédents. Cette clarification vise à sécuriser la feuille de route du modèle des « Écoles pionnières », sur lequel passe le pari de la mise à niveau de l'école publique. En apportant des garanties sur la rémunération des intervenants tout en préservant les conditions d'apprentissage des élèves, l'administration cherche à consolider l'adhésion des équipes pédagogiques sur le terrain. Autre nouveauté pour la rentrée 2026/27, le ministère lance l’expérimentation de l’« enseignant référent », avec un aménagement important de son emploi du temps : sa charge hebdomadaire d’enseignement sera réduite de moitié. À travers cette expérimentation, qui s’inscrit dans la poursuite de la feuille de route 2022-2026, notamment du programme consacré aux écoles pionnières, le ministère entend mettre en place un mode d’accompagnement pédagogique fondé sur le partage des pratiques et l’échange d’expériences entre enseignants. L’objectif est de faciliter l’appropriation des approches pédagogiques adoptées dans les écoles pionnières, sous la supervision des inspecteurs et en coordination avec les directions des établissements. L’enseignant référent sera choisi parmi les enseignants exerçant dans un collège pionnier et reconnus pour leurs compétences professionnelles et pédagogiques. La correspondance ministérielle prévoit notamment qu’il maîtrise les approches pédagogiques mises en œuvre dans ces établissements et que celles-ci aient été observées et validées par l’inspecteur pédagogique lors de ses visites d’encadrement. Le candidat devra également disposer d’une certification attestant d’un niveau d’expertise dans les approches pédagogiques concernées, faire preuve de bonnes capacités de communication et manifester une réelle disponibilité pour accompagner ses collègues et travailler en équipe. Pour permettre à l’enseignant référent d’assumer ces nouvelles responsabilités, le ministère prévoit un aménagement de son service. Il continuera à exercer ses fonctions d’enseignement, mais son emploi du temps sera organisé de manière à réduire de moitié sa charge hebdomadaire d’enseignement. Le temps ainsi dégagé devra lui permettre d’assurer ses différentes missions d’accompagnement, de formation, de coordination et de suivi auprès de ses collègues. items.title: Punjab faces greater threat from other provinces than 'neighbouring countries': CM Maryam
items.description: Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz on Saturday said the province faced a greater security threat from “neighbouring provinces than from neighbouring countries”, stressing that terrorism entered Punjab through its provincial borders. Speaking at an AI technology event in Lahore, the chief minister said, “The unfortunate thing is that the threat [Punjab] faces comes less from my neighbouring countries and more from my neighbouring provinces.” “Terrorism enters Punjab from there. Everyone has their eyes on Punjab, but, thank God, Punjab remains safe. The kind of threats we face come from all our provincial borders,” she said. The chief minister asserted that there had been a significant improvement in the law and order situation since her government came to power in 2024. She identified organised crime and religious intolerance as some of the main challenges that Punjab faced. In an apparent reference to the now-banned Tehreek-i-Labbaik Pakistan (TLP), CM Maryam said some groups “spread hatred under the cover of religion” and were “political parties in reality”. She went on to state that religious events were now held peacefully, compared to the situation of “religious polarisation” a couple of years ago. Maryam said Punjab was now the country’s “most AI-enabled province” and had invested billions of rupees in technology and security to protect and strengthen it. She said that when she assumed office, she discovered that terrorists possessed more advanced technology than the government, including night-vision cameras, and were carrying out attacks with carefully devised plans. “Thank God, we now have a complete system in place,” she said, adding that cameras had been made bulletproof because terrorists used to target them. Thermal cameras and drones had also been deployed at checkpoints and joint checkpoints to strengthen security and protect people. The Punjab CM recalled that attacks on checkpoints had previously resulted in the deaths of five people and, at times, as many as 10. “Attacks still happen, but the loss of life has been significantly reduced,” she said, attributing the improvement to investment in fortification and technology. Referring to the katcha areas , Maryam said they had previously been a hub of terrorism and crime, including kidnappings for ransom and honey traps. “With the support we have received from the military and the Punjab government, and with the cooperation of the Sindh government, the situation has now changed. The area has become largely crime-free, and the writ of the state has been established,” she declared. The chief minister also said she had decided “a few days ago” to take action against elements involved in corruption. “I am not talking about government ranks or referring to police ranks … I am talking about us as a nation. We have become so accustomed to corruption that it has become part of our daily routine,” she said. Maryam noted her government had also established a system to ensure immediate action against corrupt elements. “If people do not trust their state, that country can never move forward,” she remarked.

items.title: ‘Cleansing’ Gaza
items.description: THE Israeli defence minister has recently confirmed what many across the world already know: the Zionist state seeks to ethnically cleanse the occupied territories of their native Palestinian inhabitants. Tel Aviv seeks to achieve this reprehensible aim through murder — as witnessed in the Gaza genocide — as well as forced displacement in order to quench its insatiable thirst for other people’s land. Israel Katz has said his country is ready to depopulate Gaza and only awaits America’s green light. Israel is prepared to “get them out — by sea, by air, by every way possible”, he said, contemptuously referring to Gaza’s people as if they were livestock to be transported from one place to another. He added there was “no real solution” other than the forcible removal of Gaza’s people. In fact, there very much is a solution: Israel must vacate all occupied Palestinian territory and be made to answer for its genocidal campaign in Gaza. The situation is not much better in the West Bank. Here, the UN says Israel has forcibly displaced the residents of three refugee camps in the occupied territory. Meanwhile, rabid Jewish settlers have unleashed a reign of terror on the West Bank’s Arab population. It should be remembered that forcible displacement is a war crime, which even the so-called Gaza peace plan prohibits. Since Israel has clearly said that it only awaits America’s blessings to go ahead with the ethnic cleansing of Gaza, the Trump administration must unambiguously state its opposition to this criminal plan. In fact, those who should leave occupied Palestinian land are the Zionist military and the Israeli settlers who seek to devour Arab territory. The Palestinians have faced one Nakba already, violently forced off the land of their forefathers by outsiders. They must not be made to face another catastrophe executed by the Zionist state, and underwritten by its staunch supporters in Washington. Published in Dawn, September 5th, 2026

L’initiative est portée par la sénatrice de l’Ogou, Mme Claudine Kossiwa Otimi, avec l’appui de ses partenaires. Cette action vise à aider les orphelins et les élèves des ménages démunis à disposer des fournitures nécessaires pour reprendre les classes dans de meilleures conditions. Les kits sont composés de cahiers, de stylos, de boîtes de craie, d’ensembles géométriques et de crayons. Ils seront mis à la disposition des familles en difficulté, notamment celles identifiées et orientées par les responsables des établissements scolaires. Mme Otimi a expliqué que ce geste vise à améliorer les conditions d’apprentissage des élèves tout en contribuant à réduire les dépenses supportées par les parents à l’approche de la rentrée scolaire. « Nous mettons ces ressources à la disposition des communes afin d’alimenter les dispositifs d’aide locale. Notre priorité va à l’enseignement primaire, conformément à l’ambition nationale d’interdire qu’un enfant togolais de plus de 15 ans ne soit dépourvu du Certificat d’études du premier degré (CEPD) », a-t-elle précisé. Le maire de la commune Ogou 3, Fambo Yaovi, a salué cet appui « opportun », qui vient renforcer les efforts de la communauté éducative en faveur des enfants de familles défavorisées. items.title: ITF Juniors Tournament: Duvor Klu claims with straight-sets victory over Gakpo
items.description: Ghana’s Gwendolyn Duvor Klu has won the ITF Junior Tennis Tournament in Accra after beating Togolese player and doubles partner Winner Gakpo in straight sets. The 16-year-old produced a strong performance to win 6-2, 6-2, improving on her second-place finish at last year’s tournament. Duvor Klu admitted she was nervous at the beginning of the final, having fallen short in last year’s championship match. “I was quite nervous at the start because obviously last year, I made the final but I came second. This year, I wanted to win it,” she told JoySports. The final also presented an unusual challenge for the Ghanaian, as she lined against Gakpo, her doubles partner. “This year, I was playing against my doubles partner, so it’s a bit weird, but we still had to do it,” she added. Duvor Klu said the difference between this year’s performance and last year’s was the greater focus on tactics and having a clear plan for the match. “I was using more game plan and tactics (this year) than last year, so I had specific patterns of play and things put in place,” she explained. Despite taking control of the second set, Duvor Klu said she briefly felt the pressure when she was serving for the match at 5-1. “At the end, when I was winning the second set 5-1, I was quite nervous and it went to 5-2,” she said. She eventually held her serve to close out the match 6-2 and secure the title. “Luckily, I ended my serve and won 6-2, so I am happy,” she said. The victory adds to an important period in Duvor Klu’s young career. She recently made her senior national team debut for Ghana’s Diamond Rackets at the Billie Jean King Cup Africa Group III tournament in Botswana. The ITF Junior Tennis Tournament will run until October 10.

items.title: JI warns of nationwide wheel-jam strike unless govt provides economic relief
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) Emir Hafiz Naeemur Rehman on Saturday warned that the party would launch a nationwide wheel-jam strike if the government delayed approving public demands for economic relief. The development came two days after a countrywide protest , during which six party workers were arrested for allegedly burning motorcycles and tyres in Karachi. The JI has distanced itself from these elements. On the same day, Rehman, Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal and Prime Minister’s Adviser Rana Sanaullah announced that the JI and federal government would form committees to recommend measures for reducing the petroleum levy and providing relief to the public. Addressing a news conference in the federal capital alongside JI Deputy Chief Mian Muhammad Aslam and Islamabad Amir Nasrullah Randhawa, Rehman said formal negotiations with the government would begin on Monday, while sit-in protests across the country would continue simultaneously. He also criticised the current administration and bureaucracy, describing them as an unconstitutional “Form-47 arrangement” that was passing the burden of its inefficiency and extravagance on to the public through heavy taxation. Highlighting that the JI had protested for 21 days, with sit-ins held at dozens of locations, including 20 sites in Balochistan and Swat, Rehman maintained that public pressure had forced electricity prices down by Rs10–12 per unit, saved the national exchequer Rs4,300 billion through negotiations with IPPs, and prevented petrol prices from rising further. Addressing the national economic crisis, the JI chief said Pakistan’s total debt had reached Rs110,000bn, while annual interest payments stood at Rs8,000bn. He argued that a three per cent cut in the central bank’s policy rate would eliminate the need for the petroleum levy altogether. Criticising systemic corruption, he highlighted Rs1,300bn in annual losses due to “incompetence” at the Federal Board of Revenue and condemned continued payments to re-gasification plants even when liquefied natural gas was not being supplied. The JI chief also drew attention to governance failures in the social sector, citing a devastating fire at the state-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences and a 50pc failure rate in Punjab’s ninth-grade examinations. Rehman criticised Sindh’s key political parties, describing them as “opportunistic” and accusing them of leaving Karachi’s issues unaddressed. He said the grievances had driven residents to demand a separate province. Announcing the party’s future plans, Rehman said the JI would launch a signature campaign targeting 50 million citizens to push for structural relief, local government reforms and a reduction in bread prices to Rs10.

items.title: Zio : Le projet « Femmes leaders pour la justice et la gouvernance locale » lancé à Apéssito
items.description: Tsévié, 5 sept. (ATOP) – Le projet « Femmes leaders pour la justice et la gouvernance locale », a été lancé le vendredi 4 septembre à Apéssito, dans la commune Zio 2. Portée par l’ONG Association Vie Précieuse (AVIP-Togo), l’initiative sera mise en œuvre pendant six mois dans les communes Zio 2 et Avé 2. Elle bénéficie de l’appui technique et financier de la Coopération allemande, à travers la GIZ et son projet « DeZon ». L’objectif est de renforcer la participation sociale et politique des femmes et améliorer les pratiques en matière d’égalité juridique de traitement des femmes et des hommes dans les domaines de la législation familiale. Il s’agit également de susciter un engagement collectif en faveur de l’égalité du genre et de la participation des femmes à la gouvernance locale, d’encourager la collaboration entre femmes, hommes, chefs traditionnels, leaders religieux et autorités locales. Plusieurs activités sont prévues, notamment des formations destinées aux femmes sur le leadership, leurs droits et devoirs ainsi que sur le Code des personnes et de la famille. Les groupements de femmes seront également renforcés, tandis que des hommes seront formés sur la masculinité positive. Des dialogues communautaires réuniront par ailleurs femmes, hommes, chefs traditionnels et leaders religieux autour des questions liées aux droits et à l’épanouissement des femmes, particulièrement en milieu rural. Ces échanges devraient déboucher sur des actions de plaidoyer auprès des autorités communales. Des campagnes de sensibilisation et de communication sur les réseaux sociaux sont également prévues. La représentante du maire de la commune Zio 2, Mme Bawa Yawa Tchilalo, a estimé que ce projet vient renforcer les efforts du gouvernement en matière de promotion des droits des femmes au Togo. Elle a souligné que la prise en compte effective de la dimension genre dans les politiques et programmes locaux constitue une condition essentielle pour un développement durable et participatif. La directrice exécutive de l’AVIP-Togo, Mme Dina Agbewanou, a relevé que, malgré les avancées enregistrées au Togo en matière d’égalité entre les femmes et les hommes, les femmes restent confrontées à plusieurs obstacles qui limitent leur participation aux instances de décision et leur accès aux mécanismes de justice, particulièrement en milieu rural. Dans les communes bénéficiaires, ces difficultés sont notamment liées aux normes socioculturelles, aux inégalités d’accès aux ressources, à la faible représentation des femmes dans les espaces de décision et à la connaissance encore limitée de leurs droits et du Code des personnes et de la famille, a-t-elle expliqué. La cheffe du projet « DeZon », Mme Nkurikiye Danny, a rappelé que « DeZon » œuvre à l’amélioration des conditions institutionnelles nécessaires à la réduction des inégalités et des discriminations à l’égard des femmes et des jeunes filles. ATOP/BBG/HKM

items.title: Une 2e édition des Journées nationales de lutte antivectorielle (JNLV) pour plus de réussite
items.description: BURKINA-BOULKIEMDE-KOUDOUGOU-JNLAV-EDITION-2 Une 2e édition des Journées nationales de lutte antivectorielle (JNLV) pour plus de réussite Koudougou, 5 sept. 2026 (AIB) – La région de Nando a officiellement lancé, le samedi 4 septembre, la 2e édition des Journées nationales de lutte antivectorielle (JNLV) pour plus de réussite. Placée sous le signe de l'action citoyenne et de la salubrité publique, cette initiative de deux jours vise à réduire drastiquement l'impact du paludisme et de la dengue en s'attaquant aux gîtes larvaires des moustiques. Donnant le ton de la cérémonie, le directeur régional de la Santé de Nando, Dr Karl Mohamed Anicet Kpoda, a salué la forte mobilisation des forces vives de la région, des autorités coutumières et religieuses ainsi que des corps constitués. Il a rappelé que cette initiative se déroulera les 5 et 6 septembre autour d'un programme d'actions concrètes. Celles-ci incluent l'identification et la destruction des gîtes larvaires, le curage des caniveaux, le ramassage des pneus usagés, ainsi que des séances de pulvérisation spatiale et intradomiciliaire d'insecticides. L'objectif ultime, selon le Dr Kpoda, est d'assainir durablement le cadre de vie des populations pour barrer la route aux vecteurs de maladies. Procédant au lancement officiel au nom du gouverneur, le secrétaire général de la région, Lucien Guengueré, a quant à lui, souligné que le paludisme demeure un défi sanitaire de premier ordre. Faisant le bilan de la précédente édition, il a rappelé des acquis encourageants, notamment la collecte de 3 404 pneus usés, l'identification de 92 points verts et le curage de 3 091 mètres de caniveaux. Pour cette campagne 2026, qui compte quatre éditions majeures prévues entre mai et novembre, la stratégie régionale s'articulera autour d'axes clés. Il s’agit de la surveillance entomologique, de la mobilisation communautaire, de la gestion spécifique des pneus usagés, de l'assainissement environnemental, de la pulvérisation spatiale ciblée, de la coordination rigoureuse et du plaidoyer continu. « La lutte commence dans nos concessions, nos villages et nos quartiers. Elle est une responsabilité collective », a martelé le camarade Guengueré, invitant l'ensemble des collectivités territoriales, des organisations de la société civile et des acteurs des secteurs public et privé à s'impliquer pleinement pour débarrasser la région de ce fléau. Agence d'information du Burkina PB/AS/ATA

items.title: The Backlash Against Data Centers
items.description: Editor's Note: Washington Week With The Atlantic is a partnership between NewsHour Productions, WETA, and The Atlantic airing every Friday on PBS stations nationwide. Check your local listings , watch full episodes here , or listen to the weekly podcast here . On a special edition of Washington Week With The Atlantic , the Atlantic staff writer Josh Tyrangiel joined for a discussion about the future of AI and what, if anything, the U.S. government plans to do to address the rapid development of the technology. Across the country, massive data centers are being built, and they’re “landing themselves without a whole lot of conversation” in American towns, Tyrangiel said last night. “It’s natural that all the fears about AI—about it taking your jobs, about it rendering human beings obsolete, about the values it changes—all are focused on” these data centers, he argued. “And politicians have been incredibly late to wake up to the anger around AI.” “I don’t think people believe that they are going to partake in the wealth that comes from data centers in their community,” Tyrangiel continued. “Every community is going to make different choices, but what I’m sensing is that, particularly from Trump, the politics are out of line with where people are.” Watch Tyrangial’s full conversation with the editor in chief of The Atlantic , Jeffrey Goldberg, here .

items.title: Karachi police arrest two over alleged abduction of young man in DHA
items.description: KARACHI: Police on Saturday said they had arrested two suspects in connection with the alleged assault of a young man in DHA Phase 8. South Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Syed Asad Raza told Dawn that two of the suspects, Ibrahim Fahad and Waqar, had been arrested in connection with the case. He said a third suspect, Ibrahim Malik, had fled to Lahore, while a fourth, Irtiza, was still absconding. According to the DIG, the incident reportedly stemmed from a dispute involving a girl. The first information report (FIR), a copy of which is available with Dawn , was registered at Sahil police station in the early hours of Saturday on the complaint of Syed Ali Jafri. According to the FIR, the incident took place on the night of Aug 29. The FIR invoked sections 34 (acts done by several persons), 337-A(i) (punishment of shajjah ), 337-V( arsh for hair), 365 (kidnapping or abducting with intent secretly and wrongfully to confine person) and 506-B (criminal intimidation if threat be to cause death or grievous hurt) of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC). Jafri also spoke to the media on Saturday, recalling details of the incident and explaining that the “delay” in getting the FIR registered was because he had been threatened by the suspects against doing so. In his complaint, Jafri said he “remained silent” after the incident as he was scared, but approached the police after the suspects shared his video on social media. Jafri stated that he and his friend had gone to an e-gaming facility in Bukhari Commercial, where his friend’s acquaintance also joined them. He said he had never met the acquaintance before. The three later went to a nearby cafe and, upon leaving, were approached by a vehicle that stopped in front of them. A man, whom Jafri identified as another acquaintance of his friend, then stepped out of the vehicle. The man struck Jafri on the neck with a baseball bat, after which the friend’s acquaintance and “three unknown persons” accompanying him allegedly shoved the complainant into the vehicle and took him to an empty plot at Sahil Avenue in Phase 8, the FIR alleged. He further alleged that he was beaten on his legs with the baseball bat and that his hair was pulled, causing some of it to come out. He was then asked to “eat them”, the FIR said. Jafri said one of the unknown individuals was carrying a gun and that the attackers recorded a video of the assault. According to the FIR, he was shown pictures of his family members and threatened with similar action against them if he complained about the incident. Jafri said he was taken back to Bukhari Commercial in the same vehicle. The complainant also alleged that the suspects demanded Rs30,000 from him. By the time he reached home, he said, one of the individuals involved had already informed his family about the incident. The complainant nominated the three as suspects in the FIR. Last month, a scuffle took place in DHA’s Phase 6 between residents of two apartments, with an inquiry revealing that police officials were involved in the incident and recommending action against them.

items.title: ‘Decision to retire has been tough’ – Isaac Dogboe
items.description: Former WBO super bantamweight world champion Isaac Dogboe has revealed it was a ‘tough’ decision for him to retire from boxing. The 31-year-old announced his retirement from the sport earlier this month, calling it a quit after several years. Known as “The Royal Storm”, Dogboe made his retirement official after a spell which saw him record 24 wins and four losses, including 16 victories by knockout. According to him, that decision did not come easy as he went through troubling times. “It’s been a tough decision to make. Sometimes I’ll be there and get the itch,” he told Joy Sports. “An offer will come to the table, but I ask myself, ‘Do I really want to take this fight?’ So, I had to take a minute to arrive at this decision. “It’s never been about the money for me when it comes to boxing; I just wanted to be sure I was making the right decision.” The former world champions revealed that there were moments his mental health came in question. “It drives you nuts. Sometimes it’s a little bit deeper than it seems. Our sport or industry is such that we’re constantly portraying strength. When you’re hurt, you have to get up and act like you’re okay,” he added. “It’s difficult to find someone to talk to through all of this because you’re constantly thinking about your previous fights, your next bout…so many things running through your mind. Sometimes, combining that with family becomes difficult.”

items.description: BURKINA-BOULKIEMDE-KOUDOUGOU-CHR-INFRASTRUCTURE-REMISE-CLES CHR de Koudougou : Un nouveau bâtiment de pédiatrie offert par la république populaire de Chine augmente ses capacités d'accueil Koudougou, 5 sept. 2026 (AIB) – Le Centre hospitalier régional (CHR) de Koudougou a renforcé ses capacités d'accueil avec la réception, le vendredi 4 septembre, d'un nouveau bâtiment de pédiatrie offert par la République populaire de Chine. La cérémonie de remise officielle a été présidée par la ministre-conseillère de l'ambassade de Chine au Burkina Faso, Li Qi, représentant l'ambassadeur. Elle a remis les clés de l'infrastructure aux responsables sanitaires de la région en présence des autorités locales. D'une capacité d'accueil de 20 lits, ce nouveau joyau architectural est entièrement équipé en matériel médico-technique moderne. Le coût global de cet investissement s'élève à 40 millions de francs CFA, dont 32 millions pour les infrastructures civiles et 8 millions pour l'équipement technique. Grâce à cette acquisition, la capacité totale du CHR de Koudougou passe désormais de 299 à 319 lits. Cette réalisation majeure permettra d'améliorer significativement les conditions d'hospitalisation des jeunes patients et de leurs parents, tout en garantissant un cadre de travail optimal au personnel soignant. Exprimant sa gratitude, la directrice générale du CHR de Koudougou, Habibou Ouédraogo, a salué un acte qui transcende sa simple valeur financière. Elle y voit une marque éloquente de solidarité et un investissement stratégique pour la santé de la petite enfance. Pour sa part, la ministre-conseillère Li Qi a rappelé les liens historiques unissant les deux nations, soulignant que le CHR de Koudougou demeure l'un des tout premiers fruits de la coopération bilatérale dans les années 1980. « Il constitue un témoin historique de l'amitié sino-burkinabè », a-t-elle affirmé, avant d'ajouter que cette dynamique s'inscrit en droite ligne de la vision partagée des chefs d'État des deux pays pour le secteur de la santé. Qualifiant le nouveau bâtiment de « fleuron de la coopération sanitaire », Mme Qi s'est dite convaincue de son impact majeur sur l'amélioration des indicateurs de santé publique. La visite s'est achevée par un recueillement de la délégation chinoise au cimetière municipal de Koudougou, où un hommage mérité a été rendu aux membres des missions médicales chinoises décédés sur le sol burkinabè dans l'exercice de leurs fonctions. Agence d'information du Burkina PB/AS/ATA

items.title: Domelevo backs OSP probe into alleged GH¢70,000 payment to Appiagyei
items.description: Former Auditor-General, Daniel Yaw Domelevo, has supported the Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP) decision to investigate allegations that Deputy Minority Leader and Asokwa MP, Patricia Appiagyei, was offered GH¢70,000 in connection with the vetting of ministerial and Supreme Court nominees. Mr Domelevo believes the allegations warrant an independent investigation, particularly as claims of payments to Members of Parliament in relation to vetting exercises have surfaced on previous occasions. Speaking on Channel One TV’s The Big Issue, he said Mrs Appiagyei’s denial of the allegation should not bring the matter to an end. According to him, the OSP must establish whether the document circulating in connection with the alleged payment is genuine and whether the claims contained in it have any basis. “…But it needs to be investigated, and we’ll be sure that somebody is just being mischievous or it actually happened.” Mr Domelevo further urged the OSP to subject the disputed document to forensic examination to determine whether it was authored by the Asokwa MP and whether the signature attributed to her is authentic. He said such an examination would help establish whether Mrs Appiagyei actually signed the document or whether her signature had been forged. The former Auditor-General also raised concerns about the source of any alleged payment to MPs who participate in vetting exercises. He questioned the appropriateness of the Presidency making such payments after MPs had completed their vetting duties, arguing that this could create public financial management concerns if the expenditure was not captured in the appropriate budget. Mr Domelevo maintained that if MPs are entitled to sitting allowances for such duties, Parliament should make provision for the payments through its own budget rather than having another government institution bear the cost. He said the OSP’s investigation was therefore necessary to settle the matter and determine the authenticity of the allegations. Appiagyei denies allegation Patricia Appiagyei has, however, rejected the claims, insisting that she neither received nor discussed any money in connection with the ministerial vetting process. The Asokwa MP has described the memo alleging that GH¢70,000 was paid or offered to her as fake news. The OSP’s investigation is expected to establish the authenticity of the document and clarify the circumstances surrounding the alleged payment.

items.title: Bourse de Casablanca : performance hebdomadaire négative
items.description: La Bourse de Casablanca a clôturé la semaine du 31 août au 4 septembre dans le rouge, son indice principal, le MASI, cédant 0,73% à 18.792,25 points (pts). Le MASI.20, qui reflète la performance des cours des 20 entreprises les plus liquides, a progressé de 0,29% à 1.362,59 pts, tandis que le MASI.ESG, indice des entreprises ayant la meilleure notation ESG selon Moody’s ESG Solutions, a reculé de 1,2% à 1.393,01 pts. Le MASI Mid and Small Cap, qui mesure la performance des petites et moyennes entreprises cotées à la Bourse de Casablanca, a abandonné 0,54% à 1.805,32 pts. Sur le plan sectoriel, les indices « Ingénieries et biens d’équipement industriels » (-10,73%), « Industrie agricole » (-5,17%) et « Pharmaceutique » (-4,86%) ont accusé les plus fortes baisses. À l’opposé, les secteurs « Sociétés de placement immobilier et gestion hôtelière » (+2,52%), « Banques » (+1,52%) et « Santé » (+1,17%) ont réalisé les meilleures performances. Les échanges ont dépassé 1,68 milliard de dirhams (MMDH), réalisés essentiellement sur le marché central « Actions » et dominés par les transactions sur Managem (17,03%), Itissalat Al-Maghrib (11,64%) et Label'Vie (6,57%). La capitalisation boursière s'est établie à plus de 1.101,8 MMDH. Aux valeurs individuelles, les plus fortes progressions ont été affichées par S2M (+6,28% à 538 DH), Promopharm S.A (+6,25% à 1.377 DH), Ciments du Maroc (+4,17% à 1.750 DH), Sanlam Maroc (+3,95% à 3.000 DH) et CFG Bank (+3,69% à 208 DH). A l'inverse, les plus forts replis ont été enregistrés par Stroc Industrie (-12,68% à 179 DH), Disway (-9,08% à 701 DH), SGTM (-8,61% à 640 DH), IB Maroc.com (-8,61% à 55,01 DH), et Société des Boissons du Maroc (-6,09% à 2.005 DH). items.title: US military says it destroyed 3 Iranian oil tankers
items.description: The US military said Saturday it had struck and destroyed three oil tankers linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps after the Iranian military organization fired on American warships. “Following Iran’s failed attacks, CENTCOM permanently disabled the IRGC crude oil carriers M/T Downy off the coast of Kharg Island and M/T Stark 1 near Jask,” Central Command (CENTCOM) said in a statement on X. “American forces also completely destroyed the unladen crude oil carrier M/T Kylo… in the Gulf of Oman, striking the vessel in multiple critical locations to render it inoperable after the crew was directed to abandon ship,” it continued. Video posted by CENTCOM showed large fireballs and billowing flames after projectiles slammed into the ships. The three ships targeted were “part of a multibillion-dollar shadow network that funds the IRGC and its regional proxies,” it said. “Iran has no means by which to defend them,” it added. No US soldiers were hurt after a destroyer and aircraft carrier “successfully evaded multiple unprovoked Iranian attacks,” it said. CENTCOM’s commander, Admiral Brad Cooper, said: “Let the message to the IRGC be clear: If you shoot at two of our ships, we will impose an even higher economic cost — taking out three of yours.” The strikes come as Washington insists that it is working to economically strangle Iran, including a blockade of its ports, while keeping alive the threat of military action. Iran, for its part, has blocked commercial traffic through the critical Strait of Hormuz by threatening shipping that doesn’t have its permission to transit. The two sides exchanged fire earlier this week, with the US saying it was targeting the IRGC’s ability to attack commercial shipping while Iran fired on US military bases in nearby Jordan. AFP The post US military says it destroyed 3 Iranian oil tankers appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: FDSI–SONOCO WAQF : un partenariat de cinq ans pour renforcer la protection sociale en Guinée
items.description: Conakry, 5 septembre 2026 — La Direction Générale du Fonds de Développement Social et de l’Indigence (FDSI) et SONOCO WAQF ont officialisé, vendredi à Conakry, une convention de partenariat d’une durée de cinq ans destinée à renforcer les actions de protection sociale en Guinée. La cérémonie de signature s’est déroulée en présence de Lansana Diawara, Directeur Général du FDSI, du Directeur Exécutif de SONOCO WAQF ainsi que des cadres des deux institutions. Cette convention établit un cadre de collaboration durable autour d’actions en faveur des populations confrontées à des difficultés sociales et économiques. Ce partenariat se concentre sur deux secteurs prioritaires de la protection sociale pour améliorer les conditions de vie des populations. À travers cette collaboration, les deux institutions conjuguent leurs efforts pour concevoir, financer et déployer conjointement des programmes à fort impact social dans les domaines de la santé, de l’éducation en vue de l’autonomisation des personnes vulnérables. La mise en œuvre des différentes interventions s’appuiera sur le Registre Social Unifié (RSU), porte d’entrée unique des programmes de protection sociale en Guinée. Son utilisation permettra de mieux identifier les bénéficiaires, d’optimiser le ciblage des actions, de renforcer la coordination des interventions, tout en facilitant l’accès aux services essentiels et un accompagnement adapté adapté aux ménages qui en ont le plus besoin. Cette démarche s’inscrit dans la dynamique engagée par le Gouvernement sous l’impulsion du Président de la République, le Général Mamadi Doumbouya, pour moderniser et renforcer le système de protection sociale en Guinée. D’une durée de cinq ans, la convention traduit la volonté des deux partenaires d’inscrire leur coopération dans la durée et de développer des actions structurées dans les domaines de la santé et de l’éducation. Cette initiative permet également de saluer l’engagement de M. Abdoul Karim Diallo, Directeur Général du Groupe SONOCO et Président du Conseil d’Administration de SONOCO WAQF, dont l’accompagnement a contribué à la concrétisation de ce partenariat. À travers cette collaboration, le FDSI et SONOCO WAQF ambitionnent ainsi de contribuer au renforcement de la protection sociale en Guinée et d’en faire un véritable levier de développement humain, d’inclusion et de stabilité sociale Cellule de communication et des relations publiques L’article FDSI–SONOCO WAQF : un partenariat de cinq ans pour renforcer la protection sociale en Guinée est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Burkina: cinq individus interpellés pour usurpation d’identité, faux et usage de faux
items.description: La Brigade Centrale de Lutte Contre la Cybercriminalité (BCLCC) affirme, dans un communiqué, ce samedi 5 septembre 2026, avoir interpellé cinq présumés auteurs de faits d’usurpation d’identité, de faux et usage de faux. « Toute opération de « pré-enrôlement fictif » consistant pour des agents d’enregistrer des cartes SIM sous des identités inventées ou volée suivie de leur commercialisation, est une pratique interdite par la réglementation en vigueur. Malgré cette interdiction, certains agents malveillants enregistrent délibérément des cartes SIM sous de fausses identités moyennant rémunération, une pratique qui n’est pas sans conséquences sur le plan sécuritaire. C’est dans ce contexte que la Brigade Centrale de Lutte Contre la Cybercriminalité (BCLCC) a interpellé cinq (05) présumés auteurs de faits d’usurpation d’identité, de faux et usage de faux. Les investigations menées par la Division des enquêtes (DE) ont permis de remonter jusqu’à P.A, âgé de 23 ans, employé de commerce exerçant dans la vente de cartes SIM et de téléphones devant les locaux d’un opérateur de téléphonie de la place. P.A était régulièrement en contact avec un dénommé Kevin, tel : +229 43112878, de nationalité béninoise et résidant dans son pays, identifié comme le cerveau présumé des opérations. Ce dernier commandait depuis son pays auprès de P.A, des cartes SIM d’opérateurs de téléphonie mobile burkinabè déjà identifiées et orientait également certains de ses compatriotes vers celui-ci pour tout besoin de ce type. Pour répondre à ces demandes, P.A recevait de Kevin, via WhatsApp ou par l’intermédiaire d’autres personnes, des documents d’identité qu’il utilisait pour identifier les cartes SIM et créer des comptes Mobile Money associés aux numéros. Les cartes SIM ainsi obtenues étaient cédées au prix unitaire de deux mille (2 000) à deux mille cinq cents (2 500) francs CFA, selon la quantité commandée, puis remises aux complices ou à des intermédiaires chargés de leur acheminement. H.R, D.A, A.E et H.J, tous de nationalité béninoise, intervenaient notamment à cette étape du processus. H.R a d’ailleurs été interpellée en possession d’un colis contenant une dizaine de cartes SIM burkinabè déjà identifiées, destiné à être acheminé vers son pays. Les investigations ont par ailleurs permis d’établir qu’une vingtaine de cartes SIM avaient ainsi été mises en circulation par P.A, la plupart étant destinées à des activités d’escroquerie. Interpellés et auditionnés par la Division des enquêtes de la BCLCC, les mis en cause ont été déférés devant le camarade Procureur du Faso près le Tribunal de grande instance Ouaga I afin de répondre des faits qui leur sont reprochés. La BCLCC invite les populations à s’abstenir d’acheter ou d’utiliser toute carte SIM déjà identifiée au nom d’une autre personne. Tout cas suspect peut être signalé à la BCLCC, à son siège sis à Koulouba, par téléphone au 25 39 58 42, par courriel à l’adresse cybercrime@securite.gov.bf ou à travers la plateforme de signalement Alerte BCLCC. Votre sécurité numérique, notre mission ! » BCLCC L’article Burkina: cinq individus interpellés pour usurpation d’identité, faux et usage de faux est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .
